documents.title: Student Guidance FAQ on Generative AI
tiers: No AI use allowed (human brains only)
AI Friendly assignment (use responsibly and cite appropriately)
documents.summary: Student-facing FAQ saying Marquette has no university-wide AI policy and that instructors set rules in the syllabus, using three assignment labels. It adds a no-assumption rule when the syllabus is silent, ties unattributed or unapproved AI use to the Honor Code and plagiarism, and covers privacy, learning, and career reasons.
documents.stance_why: The FAQ states "Marquette does not have a university-wide policy" and "In general, instructors decide on AI use for your courses", and lists assignment labels ("No AI use allowed", "AI use limited", "AI Friendly assignment"); it sets no single stance and hands the decision to instructors, so delegates with tiers.

units.why: The page opens by saying Marquette "calls students to use AI tools responsibly and ethically", a general principle that frames the guidance; coded as an institution-level framework (P56) with a student actor because it addresses students, informs because it states a principle rather than a rule.
units.anchor: Marquette calls students to use AI tools responsibly and ethically.

units.why: "our Jesuit values challenge students to approach AI with discernment" states a mission-based principle for AI use; it is a framework statement (P56) rather than a harm or rationale-for-skill claim, so P53 and P41 fit less well.
units.anchor: our Jesuit values challenge students to approach AI with discernment.

units.why: "Review each course syllabus for rules on AI use" tells students the syllabus is where the rule lives, so the rule is set per course/instructor (P04); actor is student and phase course-start.
units.anchor: Review each course syllabus for rules on AI use.

units.why: The FAQ lists labels instructors may attach to assignments: "No AI use allowed", "AI use limited", "AI Friendly". Named levels of use make this P05 (tiers), not P04, which is about who decides; it informs students of the labels, so informs, neutral.
units.anchor: No AI use allowed (human brains only)
units.policy: Some instructors label assignments and assessments as no AI use allowed (human brains only), AI use limited (within guidelines), or AI Friendly (use responsibly and cite appropriately).
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all / phase general; B coded student / course-start. The sentence ('Some instructors will identify assignments...') tells students how expectations will be labelled, so it is addressed to students and is part of how expectations are communicated: student, course-start. Type P05 and informs agreed. B's normalized policy follows the source wording.

units.why: Students "uncertain about using AI" are pointed to a decision tree. This is the advice to check before using AI when unsure, so P10 fits better than P09 because it is addressed to students.
units.anchor: When assignment instructions are unclear or you are uncertain about using AI
units.frag_end: inappropriate uses of AI in your coursework.
units.policy: When assignment instructions are unclear or students are uncertain about using AI, they consult the May I Use AI for Classwork? decision tree to understand appropriate and inappropriate uses.

units.why: "Marquette does not have a university-wide policy" states that no single institutional rule exists, so the decision is left to others; P04 fits (decided per instructor) and the statement is informational.
units.anchor: Marquette does not have a university-wide policy.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded admin. The sentence is the university describing its own absence of a policy; it binds no one in particular and tells everyone who reads it, so all. Type, phase, modality agreed.

units.why: "instructors decide on AI use for your courses" hands the decision to instructors, the core of P04; it informs students who decides.
units.anchor: In general, instructors decide on AI use for your courses.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor student, B coded instructor. The sentence assigns the decision to instructors ('instructors decide on AI use'), so the party it empowers and binds is the instructor. Anchor taken from B (more complete).

units.why: "The college or department offering your course may have its own AI guidelines" adds a further layer of local rule-setting. It is a delegation of rule-setting below the university, so P04 and not P11 (which is about non-carry-over between courses).
units.anchor: The college or department offering your course may have its own AI guidelines.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor student, B coded admin. The sentence says the college or department may set its own guidelines, which is a statement about a unit's rule-setting authority, so admin. Type P04 agreed (P11 does not fit: it concerns non-carry-over between courses).

units.why: "If a tool creates or transforms your work, it's generative AI" defines what counts as AI for the guidance, which is a definition of scope (P61).
units.anchor: If a tool creates or transforms your work, it's generative AI.
units.frag_start: If a tool creates or transforms

units.why: "some long-standing software, such as word processors and spelling/grammar checkers, have revamped into AI tools" widens the definition to everyday software, so it sets scope (P61); P07 is about rules for built-in AI in editors, and this passage states no rule.
units.anchor: word processors and spelling/grammar checkers, have revamped into AI tools.
units.resolution_why: A coded P61, B coded P07. P07 covers rules about AI built into editors and agents (e.g. requiring students to disable them); this sentence states no rule about such tools, it only widens what counts as AI (the 'Note that' continues the definition above), so P61 (define scope). Anchor from A, which is shorter.

units.why: "If in doubt, check with your instructor" tells students unsure whether a tool counts as AI to ask the instructor, which is P10 (ask first).
units.anchor: If in doubt, check with your instructor.

units.why: "If allowed by your instructor, AI can help you brainstorm ideas, summarize course content" permits conditional uses; brainstorming is the lead use, so P15 rather than P14 (summaries).
units.anchor: If allowed by your instructor, AI can help you brainstorm ideas, summarize course content
units.policy: If the instructor allows it, AI can help students brainstorm ideas, summarize course content and explore new perspectives.

units.why: "AI may short-circuit your learning, if it replaces critical thinking or problem solving" warns that AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: AI may short-circuit your learning, if it replaces critical thinking or problem solving.
units.frag_start: But AI may short-circuit your learning

units.why: "AI can yield inaccurate or biased information" is a factual warning that output may be wrong, the basis of the P31 verify-output principle. The 'Keep in mind' framing states a fact rather than an instruction, so informs.
units.anchor: AI can yield inaccurate or biased information.
units.frag_start: Keep in mind that AI can
units.resolution_why: A coded modality should, B coded informs. The sentence ('Keep in mind that AI can yield inaccurate or biased information') asserts a fact and gives no instruction to check output, so informs. Type P31 and other codes agreed.

units.why: "AI misuse may lead to academic integrity issues" links misuse to the integrity process, i.e. misuse is treated as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: AI misuse may lead to academic integrity issues.

units.why: The self-check question "Is this use helping me learn or replacing the work I am meant to do?" asks students to stay the one doing the work, P32, as a should.
units.anchor: Is this use helping me learn or replacing the work I am meant to do?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether the use helps them learn or replaces the work they are meant to do.

units.why: "Does the final work still reflect my own thinking, voice and values?" asks that submitted work remain the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: Does the final work still reflect my own thinking, voice and values?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether the final work still reflects their own thinking, voice and values.

units.why: "would I feel comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor?" asks students to be ready to explain their use. It is nearest P30 (explain what you submit); P24 does not fit since no disclosure is required here.
units.anchor: would I feel comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether they would feel comfortable explaining to their instructor how they used AI.

units.why: "Struggle and effort are part of learning. AI should support learning, not skip it." is a principle that the learning practice should be kept, P41; it is a rationale, so modality should and unit_stance neutral.
units.anchor: AI should support learning, not skip it.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B coded neutral. The sentence is a rationale principle and names no restricted use, so neutral; the adjacent 'Pause before you outsource work' advice is the one that limits delegation (restrict). Type, modality agreed.

units.why: "Pause before you outsource work to AI, escaping the learning process" asks students to stop before delegating work to AI; it is about keeping the learning process, P41, and the preceding line says to seek human support first.
units.anchor: Pause before you outsource work to AI, escaping the learning process.

units.why: "Marquette recommends reaching out to campus resources" (instructor, writing center, library, ARC) directs stuck students to support before AI. No type covers support referral, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Marquette recommends reaching out to campus resources
units.policy: Marquette recommends that students feeling stuck, overwhelmed or behind reach out to campus resources (their instructor, Ott Writing Center, Raynor Library, Academic Resource Center) before turning to AI.
units.uncovered_note: Recommendation to use human campus support services (instructor, writing center, library, academic resource center) before consulting AI.

units.why: "Do not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into public AI tools" is a data-protection prohibition (P50).
units.anchor: Do not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into public AI tools.

units.why: "may lose control of your data" explains that public tools can reuse entered data; it supports the privacy rule, P50, as information.
units.anchor: may lose control of your data
units.policy: Students may lose control of their data when they enter it into a public AI tool, which could reuse it to answer questions asked by anyone else.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded during-work. The sentence is an explanatory fact ('Know that you may lose control of your data') supporting the preceding rule rather than an action at a point in the work, so general. Type, actor, modality agreed.

units.why: "Follow guidance from your instructor or faculty researcher on approved and supported AI tools" tells students to use only approved, supported tools as directed, matching P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: Follow guidance from your instructor or faculty researcher on approved and supported AI tools.

units.why: "not all AI platforms protect your data in the same way" is a privacy fact that supports choosing vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: not all AI platforms protect your data in the same way.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded during-work. The sentence is an informing fact about platforms, so general, consistent with the adjacent data-control fact.

units.why: "Start with the AI Tool List, noting which tools are available to students" points students to a university list of available tools, P17 (sanctioned tools).
units.anchor: noting which tools are available to students
units.policy: Students start with the AI Tool List, noting which tools are available to them.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance encourage, B coded neutral. Pointing students to the list of available tools directs them to sanctioned tools but does not itself welcome AI use, so neutral. B's normalized policy follows the source.

units.why: "Ask your instructor before using AI for your classwork" is the action when the syllabus is silent, P10 (ask first), distinct from the fallback rule below.
units.anchor: Ask your instructor before using AI for your classwork.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase course-start, B coded during-work. The instruction applies when a student is about to use AI for classwork and the syllabus is silent ('before using AI for your classwork'), so the act it governs is during-work; the next line (the fallback rule P06) is course-start. Type P10, must, restrict agreed.

units.why: "Don't assume omission of AI from the syllabus means you can use AI" sets what applies when the syllabus is silent: no assumed permission, i.e. the fallback rule (P06).
units.anchor: Don't assume omission of AI from the syllabus means you can use AI.

units.why: "Using AI (without instructor approval) is not individual work" ties unapproved AI use to an Honor Code breach ("neither to accept nor give unauthorized help"), i.e. classes it as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Using AI (without instructor approval) is not individual work.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase when-misuse, B coded during-work. The sentence classes unapproved AI use as a breach of the Honor Code's individual-work rule, i.e. it states what counts as misconduct, in the same way as the plagiarism line that follows, so when-misuse. Other codes agreed.

units.why: "submitting AI work as your own is plagiarism" classifies undisclosed AI work as plagiarism, handled under integrity processes, P36.
units.anchor: Yes, submitting AI work as your own is plagiarism.

units.why: The quoted Academic Misconduct Policy defines plagiarism as "lacking or unclear attribution of content developed with generative software", making unattributed AI content misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: lacking or unclear attribution of content developed with generative software
units.policy: Plagiarism includes the use of another's creations or ideas without proper attribution, including lacking or unclear attribution of content developed with generative software ('artificial intelligence').
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all / phase general with a normalized policy; B coded student / when-misuse with null policy. The quoted University Academic Misconduct Policy is a definition of plagiarism that applies to everyone, so actor all and phase general (definitions). A's normalized policy is kept since the shorter anchor alone does not state the full rule.

units.why: "To avoid academic misconduct, disclose and attribute AI use" directly requires disclosure and attribution (P24) as the way to stay within integrity rules.
units.anchor: To avoid academic misconduct, disclose and attribute AI use.

units.why: "You are obliged to report any observed breaches of this honor code" requires students to report peers' misconduct; no type covers reporting by other students.
units.anchor: to report any observed breaches of this honor code and academic honesty.
units.frag_start: The Honor Code is clear. You
units.policy: Students are obliged to report any observed breaches of the honor code and academic honesty.
units.uncovered_note: Students are obliged to report observed honor-code breaches by other students (peer reporting).
units.resolution_why: A split the peer-reporting passage into two units (the duty; the anonymous form option), B merged them into one. The duty to report and the reporting channel are two distinct rules, so the duty is kept here and the channel is a separate unit. Both coders marked UNCOVERED, must, when-misuse.

units.why: "Your instructor specifies which citation style to use for attribution" says how AI attribution is done, left to the instructor; it belongs with disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: Your instructor specifies which citation style to use for attribution.

units.why: "Using AI in ways not permitted by your instructor may violate Marquette's academic integrity policies" links unpermitted use to integrity violations (P36); 'may violate' states a consequence, not a command, so informs, with unit_stance restrict because it limits use to what the instructor permits.
units.anchor: Using AI in ways not permitted by your instructor may violate
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded must-not. The sentence says unpermitted use 'may violate' the integrity policies, a statement of consequence rather than a prohibition issued in this sentence, so informs. Type P36 and unit_stance restrict agreed.

units.why: "It's important to follow each instructor's direction about AI in your course" makes the instructor the authority for each course (P04).
units.anchor: follow each instructor's direction about AI in your course.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase course-start, B coded during-work. 'It's important to follow each instructor's direction about AI in your course' is a standing instruction applying while students do the work, so during-work. Other codes agreed.

units.why: "learning how to use AI responsibly now prepares you to" collaborate, justify decisions and act with social responsibility: a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: learning how to use AI responsibly now prepares you to
units.frag_start: At Marquette, learning how to use
units.policy: At Marquette, learning to use AI responsibly prepares students to collaborate effectively with technology, explain and justify their decisions, and use tools in ways that honor human dignity and social responsibility.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral with null policy, B coded encourage with a normalized policy. The passage gives a reason for learning responsible use (a rationale, P44) and does not itself urge more AI use, so neutral. B's normalized policy is kept because it carries all three outcomes in the list; A's separate unit for the third bullet is dropped as part of this same rationale.

units.why: "AI will be part of many professions you enter after graduation" is a career rationale that responsible AI use is a professional skill (P44).
units.anchor: AI will be part of many professions you enter after graduation.

units.why: "Employers expect not just technical skill but judgment, ethics and accountability" states what employers want, a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: Employers expect not just technical skill but judgment, ethics and accountability.

units.why: "AI can be a helpful learning tool, but it is not a substitute for your thinking" states that the student stays the thinker (P32); it is a statement of principle without an instruction, so informs.
units.anchor: it is not a substitute for your thinking.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality should, B coded informs. The sentence is a statement of what AI is and is not, with no imperative, so informs. Type P32 agreed.

units.why: "Your instructors set expectations; when unsure, ask" repeats the ask-first advice in the takeaways, P10.
units.anchor: Your instructors set expectations; when unsure, ask.
units.resolution_why: Found by B only. The takeaway 'Your instructors set expectations; when unsure, ask' is a real instruction that restates the ask-first advice in the takeaway list in different words (not an exact repeat); kept as P10.

units.why: "Reflect on how AI use affects your learning and integrity" asks for self-reflection; closest to P32 (student keeps charge of own learning). It is not a submitted reflection, so not P26.
units.anchor: Reflect on how AI use affects your learning and integrity.
units.resolution_why: Found by B only. The takeaway 'Reflect on how AI use affects your learning and integrity' is a real recommendation to students; closest type P32 (student stays in charge of own learning). Kept.

units.why: "Use AI in ways that align with Marquette's values" states a general principle for use, P56.
units.anchor: Use AI in ways that align with Marquette
units.policy: Students use AI in ways that align with Marquette's values and their own growth.
units.resolution_why: Found by B only. 'Use AI in ways that align with Marquette's values and your own growth' is a real principle in the takeaways; P56 (institution-level principles). Kept.

units.why: "The form includes an option to remain anonymous" describes how peers can report suspected misuse via the Academic Misconduct Report Form; peer reporting channel is not covered by any type.
units.anchor: The form includes an option to remain anonymous.
units.frag_start: If you are comfortable, discuss the
units.policy: Students may discuss observed academic misconduct with their instructor or submit an Academic Misconduct Report Form, which includes an option to remain anonymous.
units.uncovered_note: Channel for students to report suspected misconduct, including anonymous reporting.
units.resolution_why: Found by A only as a separate unit (B folded it into the duty-to-report unit). It is a distinct rule, the reporting channel with an anonymous option, so it is kept as its own UNCOVERED unit with a normalized policy that includes the instructor route stated just before it.

documents.title: AI, Generative and Emerging Technologies Support for the Classroom
documents.summary: Center for Teaching and Learning page for instructors stating Marquette has no unified AI policy and encouraging instructors to tell students their own expectations. It lists related guidance documents and offers department presentations and videos; the page itself does not set a stance.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility" and asks instructors to articulate "what you encourage, what you prohibit, and what you find acceptable", so it sets no stance itself and delegates.

units.why: "Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility" says there is no single policy and that flexibility is preferred, so instructors decide (P04).
units.anchor: Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded before-course. The sentence is a statement of the university's position (no unified policy), a general principle rather than something done at the design stage, so general.

units.why: "your college or department may have its own guidelines" notes that rules can also be set at college or department level, a who-decides statement (P04).
units.anchor: your college or department may have its own guidelines
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded before-course. Same reasoning as the previous unit: a statement about who may set rules, general.

units.why: "students need and deserve clear articulations of what your expectations are" tells instructors to state their AI expectations; it addresses instructors before the term and corresponds to P09.
units.anchor: students need and deserve clear articulations of what your expectations are
units.policy: Instructors give students clear articulations of their expectations on AI (what they encourage, what they prohibit, what they find acceptable) and why.

units.why: "Recommended communication with students can be found below" points instructors to suggested syllabus language and visuals for communicating AI expectations (P09).
units.anchor: Recommended communication with students can be found below.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded should. The sentence only says recommended wording 'can be found below'; it points to resources and gives no instruction, so informs.

units.why: "offers customized sessions on AI resources, responsible use, course design considerations, and department-level discussions" is support for faculty to learn about AI and plan policy (P63).
units.anchor: offers customized sessions on AI resources, responsible use, course design considerations
units.frag_start: The Center for Teaching and Learning,
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance encourage, B coded neutral. The sentence announces a service the CTL offers and does not urge AI use, so neutral.

units.why: The "Our Favorite Things" video series features faculty and students "reflecting on how they are both discerning and may be engaging AI", supporting faculty in learning from peers (P63).
units.anchor: reflecting on how they are both discerning and may be engaging AI
units.frag_end: Ignatian Pedagogy and our Jesuit mission.

units.why: The CTL and a librarian offer help with "how to design your assignments in light of it" and discussing AI with students, which is support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: how to design your assignments in light of it
units.frag_start: For help learning more about AI
units.policy: The CTL and the Digital Scholarship Librarian help instructors learn about AI, discuss it with students, and design assignments in light of it.
units.resolution_why: Found by B only. The page offers CTL and librarian help with 'how to design your assignments in light of it' and discussing AI with students; this is support for faculty (P63), a real statement. Kept.

documents.title: Academic Integrity
documents.summary: Provost academic integrity page. On AI it asks instructors to talk to students before filing an allegation, to give specific examples of unattributed generative material, and to treat AI detectors as unreliable. It sets no stance on AI use itself.
documents.stance_why: The page gives only integrity-process guidance (e.g. "AI detectors offer both false positives and false negatives") and no rule on whether students may use AI, so it sets no stance and delegates.

units.why: "We encourage all instructors to speak with their students about potential allegations before submission" asks instructors to talk with the student before filing a report, which is P57.
units.anchor: speak with their students about potential allegations

units.why: "Ignatian pedagogy is founded on person-to-person presence" is the stated reason for talking with students before reporting, so it explains P57.
units.anchor: Ignatian pedagogy is founded on person-to-person presence.
units.resolution_why: Found by A only. 'Ignatian pedagogy is founded on person-to-person presence' is the stated reason for the preceding request to talk to students; it explains P57, a rationale statement in the policy text. Kept.

units.why: "please ensure that your report includes explicit rationales with specific examples" sets what an AI-related misconduct report should contain. It is a requirement on the report within the integrity process (P36); P40 is about tools and evidence used to identify misuse, which this is not. 'please' makes it should.
units.anchor: ensure that your report includes explicit rationales with specific examples
units.policy: If an allegation includes suspicion of unattributed use of generative software, the report includes explicit rationales with specific examples of the suspected unattributed material.
units.resolution_why: A coded P36 / must, B coded P40 / should. The sentence tells instructors what a misconduct report should contain; it is a reporting procedure within the integrity process (P36 handled by integrity processes), not a detection tool or process evidence (P40). 'please ensure' is a request, so should. B's normalized policy is kept.

units.why: "AI detectors offer both false positives and false negatives" and their findings as evidence "are less reliable", so detectors should not be relied on alone, P39.
units.anchor: AI detectors" offer both false positives and false negatives
units.policy: AI detectors offer both false positives and false negatives, so their findings as evidence of misconduct are less reliable in the absence of other evidence.
units.resolution_why: A coded should-not / restrict with null policy, B coded informs / neutral with a policy. The sentence ('Please note: ... less reliable in the absence of other evidence') states that detector findings are less reliable and does not forbid their use, so informs and neutral. Type P39 agreed. B's policy is kept.

notes: Responsible-use ITS PDF was screened exclude and not coded. No school, computing or course documents found for Marquette. Two UNCOVERED themes (both coders): referral to human campus support before AI, and peer-reporting of honor-code breaches (duty plus anonymous channel).
